drives.description: A compact solid-core fission drive that exceeds the efficiency of chemical rockets but lacks their thrust.
The Nuclear Engine for Rocket Vehicle Applications solid-core fission design is suitable for interplanetary journeys.
An enhanced, compact solid-core nuclear fission rocket.
A solid-core fission rocket with improved thrust over earlier designs.
A Nerva variant using highly enriched uranium to reduce mass and increase thrust and efficiency.
An improved Nerva drive with a significant increase in thrust.
A solid-core fission rocket that operates at higher temperatures and produces more thrust than Nerva designs.
A powerful Nerva drive with reduced waste heat.
A Dumbo variant with the highest thrust we believe we can achieve with solid-core fission systems.
Solid-core fission drive that dumps superheated propellant in pulses to amplify thrust.
Upgraded Pulsar Drive design that offers excellent efficiency for a solid-core fission drive.
Propellant is run through a bed of small spheres composed of graphite and nuclear fuel, operating at temperatures that allow high thrust.
A fission drive with a rotating reactor dumps spent fuel modules, reducing the need for radiators.
Liquified fissioning uranium is spun around a stream of hydrogen, heating it as it is expelled through a nozzle.
A mist of fissioning uranium heats hydrogen propellant.
Propellant is injected into a rotating nuclear core of liquid refractory metals.
An advanced version of the Fission Spinner drive that offers incredible amounts of thrust.
Propellant is pumped through a controlled meltdown of uranium hexafluoride vapor to provide thrust.
Improved heat containment and propellant control in this gas core design allow higher thrust.
Fissioning uranium gas is held in massive pressures in an amorphous silica bulb while its radiation heats propellant.
An array of cells containing vaporized uranium cores allows for high thrust.
A chamber of quartz confines uranium plasma as hydrogen propellant is heated and expelled.
The gas core fission lightbulb improves on the Quartz Drive design for higher thrust and efficiency.
Enhanced fission lightbulb suitable for deep space missions.

drives.notes: Gas Core NTR closed 2 Max EV
drives.description: High-power nuclear gas core drive capable of extremely high thrust for a fission regime.
Weak but efficient nuclear drive directly expels fissioned atoms as reaction mass.
Fission fragment drive variant that uses ground fission fuel for improved efficiency.
Hydrogen seeded with tungsten dust is pushed through fission plasma to provide thrust.
Americium-241 replaces uranium for a more efficient reaction in this advanced gas core drive.
The most powerful gas core fission rocket we can design.
A powerful drive relying on a steady nuclear detonation using enriched uranium tetrabromide.
An advanced nuclear salt water rocket that can go anywhere in the Solar System and beyond.
Tiny curium bomblets are detonated to propel a ship.
Free neutrons bombard Lithium-6 to induce fission.
Tiny amounts of antimatter induce small fission explosions that propel a ship.
Magnetically compressed fissiles produce low-yield nuclear explosions, pushing a ship forward.
Improved utilization of energy from nuclear explosions offer increased thrust and efficiency for our Mini-Mag Orion drive design.
They said it was madness, but the dream of detonating nuclear bombs to push a ship through space can be realized.
If fission bombs can make our ships go places, why can't thermonuclear warheads?
